sections.h2: What the Brunswick County Register of Deeds handles
sections.html:
Land records for the whole county are kept here. Deeds, deeds of trust, easements, maps, releases and satisfactions pass through the office, as do marriage licenses, certified copies and oaths. Voters choose the register for a four-year term. The staff can file what you bring but cannot advise you or draft the paper.

Other filings include restrictions and covenants, assumed names, UCC statements and powers of attorney, on top of the steady flow of deeds from coastal home sales. A seller reaches this counter in person, by mail or through a title firm. Until the buyer's deed is on the record, the sale is not protected against outside claims.

Find the office in Building I at 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422. The phone is 910-253-2690, with 877-625-9310 as the toll-free alternate, and mail is addressed to PO Box 87 in Bolivia. Services run on separate schedules.

  • Recording desk: opens 8:30 am, closes 4:30 pm, weekdays.
  • Land and vital records: opens 8:30 am, closes 5 pm, weekdays.
  • Marriage licenses: by appointment, 8:30 am until 4:30 pm.
  • Passports: by appointment, 8:30 am until 3:30 pm.

You can hand a document over at the counter, post it to the box, or ship it by courier to the Courthouse Drive street address. The county holiday calendar applies to the recording desk.

sections.h2: What the county requires before recording a deed
sections.html:
The clerks work from a short county checklist. They accept only an original, or a certified copy bearing the original signature.

  • A check to BCROD for the recording fee, with a stamped return envelope.
  • Page one shows who prepared the deed and where to reach them.
  • Seller and buyer both appear on the face of the deed, each with an address.
  • Signatures and a notary seal that reads clearly.
  • The delinquent tax certification step the county lists for all deeds.
  • Excise tax, which the county words as $2 for every $1,000 of sales price.

Layout counts too. The county quotes G.S. 161-14(b), which calls for letter or legal paper, a three-inch blank band on page one, half-inch margins on the rest, black ink on white in 9 points or larger, and printing on one side only. A deed that misses these limits is still taken, with $25 added.

Prices come from a statewide schedule plus the county's own copy rates.

Charges tied to a Brunswick County deed
Document or serviceCharge
General instrument$26.00 buys up to 15 pages; each extra page is $4.00
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 buys up to 35 pages; each extra page is $4.00
Mortgage satisfactionFree
Paper that breaks the format standards$25.00 added
Certified copy$5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page
Plain copy25 cents per page; by mail, add $1.00 or send a stamped envelope
Excise tax$1.00 for every $500 of value

Plats have their own price. A freestanding plat on film or mylar must be 18 by 24 inches and approved by the county review officer; the state schedule charges $21.00 per sheet.

It falls on the seller. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor pays the register before the deed is recorded: one dollar for each $500 of value, with a leftover fraction counted as a full $500. County government keeps half of every collection and passes the other half to the state.

Unpaid property tax is its own obstacle. The county makes tax certification a condition of recording, and a deed filed electronically has to say the closing attorney will pay any delinquent taxes to the county tax collector when funds go out. If you owe taxes, get a payoff figure from the collector early, and ask your attorney to show the excise line on the settlement statement.

Lenders and other businesses may e-record through Internet Technologies, Inc. (Inttek) in the normal weekday recording hours, while private owners usually file on paper.

  • Paying by card or PayPal adds 6% of the document's total cost plus $0.50.
  • Sending ACH funds into escrow adds 2.5% of the escrowed amount.
  • The vendor charge is on top of the regular recording fees.
  • A map can be e-recorded if it shows an existing parcel.

A deed recorded this way has to begin with a prepared-by statement naming a North Carolina attorney, plus the delinquent tax wording, and every e-filing carries the submitter statement tied to the county's submitter agreement. Ask your closing firm which route it takes. Many deeds reach the office the day they are signed through e-filing.

sections.h2: How to search deeds and get copies
sections.html:
Online records start with September 1939 filings. Enter just one detail, whether a buyer's name, a date range, a document type or a book and page, and every result can be downloaded as a PDF.

Index books for 1932 to 1953 are scanned as legacy indexes: find the name alphabetically, then key the book and page into the search page. A certified copy can be ordered by mailing a written request and payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or through the search site.

A redaction form lets anyone ask the office to blank out a Social Security, bank or card number on an image posted online. There is also a free fraud alert that notifies you whenever a document is recorded under your name, handy for owners of vacant or inherited houses.

sections.h2: Why recording matters when you sell
sections.html:
Recording decides who stands first among competing claims. G.S. 47-18 gives an unregistered conveyance no weight against lien creditors or paying buyers, and priority follows the time of registration.

So the buyer's attorney holds the money until the deed and new loan papers are filed. On your side, an old mortgage should show a recorded satisfaction. The lender files it, the county charges nothing, and a quick search of your own deed confirms it is there.

Inherited houses, liens and unpaid taxes slow the process, so raise them with the closing attorney early. A cash buyer's offer still needs the same deed, the same tax certification and the same excise payment.

sections.h2: A seller's checklist for closing day
sections.html: Have the closing attorney confirm three things on the deed itself: both parties named with addresses, a notary seal that reads clearly, and the preparer's name on page one. Confirm the tax certification is done, the excise payment is on the settlement statement, and the recording fee check is made out to BCROD. If the deed will be e-recorded, check that the prepared-by statement and delinquent tax wording are in place.

faqs.q: Where does a Brunswick County deed get filed?
faqs.a: At Building I, 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422, or by mail to PO Box 87. Recording hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone is 910-253-2690.

faqs.q: How is the Brunswick County deed stamp tax figured?
faqs.a: The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value conveyed, a figure the county also words as $2 per $1,000, and the seller pays it up front.

faqs.q: What is the fee to file a mortgage in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: State law sets $64.00 through page 35 and $4.00 for each page beyond. Filing the satisfaction after payoff is free.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner e-record a Brunswick County deed?
faqs.a: Only businesses and lenders can, through Inttek. Vendor fees run 6% plus $0.50 for cards or 2.5% for ACH escrow, in addition to normal recording fees.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified deed copy from Bolivia?
faqs.a: Mail a written request with payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or click the request link in the online search results. Page one is $5.00 and later pages are $2.00 each.
